judgments.reasoning_cat1: Coverage turns on 'Forgery or alteration of a Financial Instrument', and the enumerated examples (a)-(c) are all paper checks and drafts, raising an ejusdem generis question whether anything outside those specifics qualifies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reach depends entirely on the definitions of Forgery (c071) and Financial Instrument (c070) and is cut back by c107 and c105(a), so the clause cannot be applied without reconciling those.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line grant whose whole content is the phrases 'direct loss', 'resulting from Computer Fraud' and 'committed by a Third Party' — each a term the parties can and do read very differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It incorporates c060, c062 and c061, whose narrow 'Computer System' ownership requirement and 'fraudulent entry of Data' language may not fit the broad coverage the insuring clause appears to promise, and c125's data-breach carve-back excepts only Insuring Clause 6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Everything depends on 'direct loss' and the defined phrase 'Funds Transfer Fraud', including whether an instruction 'purportedly issued by an Organization' covers an instruction an employee actually sent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with c072's 'without such Organization's knowledge or consent' and with c052's overlapping computer fraud grant, and c125 singles this clause out for a carve-back from the data-breach exclusions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short grant referring to a tightly drawn definition of money-order and counterfeit-currency fraud.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with c078's definition and with the exception in c100 for Insuring Clause 7; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short grant keyed to the defined term Credit Card Fraud; little independent content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion 18 (c109) excludes loss from 'any forgery or alteration of, on or in any written instrument' — the very thing c064 defines Credit Card Fraud to be — so the grant and the exclusion nearly cancel out absent the (a)/(b) provisos.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Not in collusion with such Client's employees' is a determinate qualifier; 'direct loss' remains the softest term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with c059 (Client), c088 (Theft) and the ownership rule in c111's second paragraph without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The last sentence ('No Retention shall apply') sits awkwardly beside the condition that the underlying loss exceed the applicable Retention, though the two are reconcilable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reads with c076, c063 and the exception in exclusion 12(g) (c096) preserving these expenses; those cross-references are accurate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Similar financial institution' is an open-ended catch-all following two specifics, but of narrow practical consequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in c049 (Premises Coverage) and consistent with exclusion 12(m) (c102) on custody by banks.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines Client by written contract or fee, a bright line.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with c056, c076 and c063's exclusion of Client expenses; no inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unlawful taking or the fraudulently induced transfer' and the requirement that it 'result from' a Computer Violation are precisely the words on which a computer-fraud coverage dispute turns.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its meaning is entirely parasitic on c062 and c061, and it must be squared with the 'direct loss' language of c052 and the consequential-loss exclusion c096.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Owned and operated or leased and operated by an Organization' is a narrow and contestable qualifier when applied to hosted or third-party e-mail and cloud systems.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restricts c062 and hence c052, potentially defeating the computer-fraud grant altogether for systems the insured uses but does not own — a live whole-instrument tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Fraudulent entry of Data into ... a Computer System' and the trailing qualifier 'directed against an Organization' are ambiguous in scope, including whether the trailing phrase attaches to (c) alone or to all three limbs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplies the operative content of c060 and c052 and depends on c061 and c065, so any mismatch among those definitions decides coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable expenses' is standard and the definition is otherwise itemised and bounded by a consent requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the grant in c057(b) and the exception in c096; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined by reference to Forgery of a written instrument 'required in connection with any credit card'; the word 'required' is a little loose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits directly against exclusion 18 (c109), which excludes loss caused by forgery of any written instrument under the same Insuring Clause 8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A representation of information, knowledge, facts, concepts or instructions which are processed and stored in a Computer System' is broad and its application to e-mail content or embedded code is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the hinge of c062 and therefore of the computer-fraud grant in c052, and it is constrained by c061's ownership requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Uses a reasonable-person standard and a knowledge-imputation carve-out; workable but inherently fact-sensitive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives the triggers in c110/c127/c134 and c130, which have been amended inconsistently by two endorsements, so what must be 'Discovered' and when is unsettled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A four-limb definition using 'regular service', 'ordinary course' and a right-to-govern test; broad but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with c069 (Executive, as amended by c122), c089 (Third Party) and exclusion 13(a) (c104) on agents and independent contractors, which cut in the opposite direction but are expressly drawn.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined by direct reference to Title 1 of ERISA; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with c074 and c112; the parallel c079 (Non-ERISA Plan) is defined but barely used elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Equivalent positions' in foreign-chartered organizations is an open-ended catch-all, though the enumerated roles are specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subparagraph (a) is replaced in its entirety by Endorsement 1 (c122) to add 'trustee', so the policy as printed states a superseded text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A check, draft or similar written promise, order or direction to pay a sum certain in Money' pairs specifics with a catch-all whose reach to electronic instructions or e-mails is precisely what parties fight about.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs the scope of c051 and c113(a), and overlaps uneasily with c072, which covers electronic 'instructions' expressly other than Forgery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Signing of the name of another natural person or organization, with the intent to deceive' plus the electronic-signature sentence raises a genuine question whether a spoofed electronic identifier is a 'signature'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its meaning determines c051 and interacts with c072's parenthetical excluding Forgery from Funds Transfer Fraud, so the two definitions must be drawn against each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Purportedly issued by an Organization' and 'without such Organization's knowledge or consent' are the operative and contestable phrases where an employee was deceived into authorising the transfer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with c053, with the Forgery exclusion in its own parenthetical (c071), and with c125's proviso preserving Insuring Clause 6 alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Designated to represent an Insured for the purpose of effecting and maintaining insurance' is reasonably specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in c066 and c104(b); consistent usage throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and closed: any Organization, plus plans for Insuring Clause 1 only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The insuring clauses alternate between 'sustained by an Insured' and 'sustained by an Organization' and always pay the Parent Organization, an inconsistency of usage a court may have to smooth.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines start and end of conveyance with precision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with c050 and with exclusion 14(b) (c105) on carriers for hire.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable expenses' subject to prior written consent; standard and bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Aligns with c057(a) and the carve-out in c096.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Currency, coin, bank notes and bullion' is a closed physical list, which invites argument that funds held or transferred electronically are not 'Money'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Insuring Clauses 5 and 6 (c052, c053) cover loss of Money by electronic fraud, so the physical-only definition sits uncomfortably with the coverage those clauses appear to grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two enumerated situations with concrete conditions; little scope for dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches c054 and the carve-out in c100; limited to US and Canadian currency, which sits against the worldwide territory clause c014.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mirror image of the ERISA Plan definition, defined by statute; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Non-ERISA Plan appears in c074 but the ERISA-specific machinery in c112 says nothing about such plans, leaving their treatment underspecified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely referential to Item 4 of the Declarations; no ambiguity in the words themselves.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 4 reads 'Medidate Solutions, Inc., and its subsidiaries' — a misspelling and an open-ended class that must be read with the Subsidiary definition (c087) and Changes in Exposure (c114/c128).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Interior portion of a building occupied by an Organization in conducting its business' is concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in c049, c075, c084 and c111(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Tangible property other than Money or Securities' is short but definite, though its application to data or software is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Computer Fraud (c052) covers loss of Property while c063 treats data restoration as an expense, so intangible data is handled elsewhere rather than inconsistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed elements (violence or threat, presence and cognizance) with an express exception for watchmen and janitors.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with c049, c050 and the extortion exclusion c106's 'as distinct from Robbery'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires forcible entry 'evidenced by visible marks'; a bright evidentiary line.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in c049 and in the fire exclusion carve-back c099(ii); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An inclusive list of compensation components; 'including' leaves the edges open but the core is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in c067, c076, c063 and the trading-loss proviso c090; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains an evident mechanical error ('nor-negotiable' for non-negotiable), and 'contracts representing either Money or Property' is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with c077's physical definition of Money and with the valuation rules in c119(a); no direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A quantified more-than-50% control test; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with c114/c128 (Changes in Exposure) and Item 4's 'and its subsidiaries' designation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unlawful taking ... to the deprivation of' is compact and its application to funds voluntarily transferred by a deceived employee is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with exclusion 12(k) (c100) on knowingly surrendering Money and with c048, the boundary between theft and induced transfer is left to be worked out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined only negatively by reference to Employee and collusion, which forces every 'Third Party' question back through c067.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Insuring Clauses 5 and 6 require a Third Party while the loss is executed through employees, so the definition's fit with c052/c053 can be decisive.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Resulting directly or indirectly from any authorized or unauthorized trading' is very broad, with a detailed proviso limiting the carve-back.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its proviso is keyed accurately to Insuring Clause 1 and c085's Salary definition; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Other confidential information of any kind' is an unbounded catch-all after two specifics, a textbook general-versus-specific problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement/Rider 2 (c124) deletes Exclusion 12(b) outright and substitutes c125, so the printed exclusion no longer forms part of the contract.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed arithmetic proviso tied to ownership percentage and audited statements; complex but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with c069(d) (partner as Executive) and c066's Discovery date; no contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Governmental intervention' and 'any act or condition incident to any of the foregoing' extend a specific list with an open catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision qualifies the war exclusion; the trade-sanctions endorsement c045 is separate and compatible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard nuclear exclusion with a familiar incident-to tail.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Stands alone; nothing elsewhere grants nuclear-related coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Loss of income not realized as the result of a covered loss' is compressed to the point that the negative is hard to parse.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps with the consequential-loss exclusion c096 and with the 'direct loss' language of the insuring clauses, all pointing the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Indirect or consequential loss or damage of any kind' is broad and its boundary against covered loss is a classic construction battleground.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines the negative of the 'direct loss' requirement in c048-c056, and its only carve-back is for Insuring Clause 10 expenses, so causation disputes under c052/c053 run through it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four itemised categories of data-related expense; concrete though technical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits against the Computer Violation Expenses grant in c057(b)/c063, which it narrows rather than contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple exclusion of litigation costs with an express proviso pointing to Subsection 22.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-reference to c113 is accurate, so the two operate together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sub-paragraph is mislabelled '(i)' where the text refers to Exclusion 12(j), a mechanical error, though the substance is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-backs correctly track c077 (Money), c086 (Securities) and c084 (Safe Burglary).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Knowingly having given or surrendered' in an 'exchange or purchase' is exactly the voluntary-parting language over which insurers and insureds divide in fraud-induced payment cases.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its provisos preserve Insuring Clause 7 and Property loss under Insuring Clause 5 but not Insuring Clause 6, so it can be argued to swallow part of the funds-transfer grant in c053.
